1-creative-thinking.title: Creative Thinking
1-creative-thinking.summary: Generating novel approaches and solutions; not constrained by established patterns. The ability to think beyond 'how it has always been done' to discover new ways of addressing business needs.

2-decision-making.title: Decision Making
2-decision-making.summary: Applying systematic criteria to choose among options under uncertainty. Decision making involves identifying the decision, gathering information, evaluating alternatives, and committing to a course of action.

3-learning.title: Learning
3-learning.summary: Rapidly acquiring domain knowledge and adapting to new contexts. Learning is the engine of professional growth — absorbing new business domains, methodologies, technologies, and stakeholder languages.

4-problem-solving.title: Problem Solving
4-problem-solving.summary: Identifying root causes (not just symptoms), then generating and evaluating solutions. Problem solving is the practical application of analytical thinking to real-world business challenges.

5-systems-thinking.title: Systems Thinking
5-systems-thinking.summary: Understanding how components interrelate within a whole system. Systems thinking avoids local optimizations that create global problems by considering the full context and ripple effects of change.

6-conceptual-thinking.title: Conceptual Thinking
6-conceptual-thinking.summary: Identifying patterns, principles, and abstract concepts from specific instances. Conceptual thinking enables the BA to recognize recurring structures across different business domains and apply known solutions to novel problems.

7-visual-thinking.title: Visual Thinking
7-visual-thinking.summary: Using visual representations to explore, analyze, and communicate ideas. Visual thinking leverages diagrams, models, sketches, and prototypes to make abstract concepts tangible and accessible.

8-ethics.title: Ethics
8-ethics.summary: Acting with integrity — maintaining confidentiality, managing conflicts of interest, and upholding professional standards. Ethics is the foundation of trust between the BA and all stakeholders.

9-personal-accountability.title: Personal Accountability
9-personal-accountability.summary: Taking ownership of commitments, deliverables, and outcomes. Personal accountability means following through on promises and taking responsibility for results — including mistakes.

10-trustworthiness.title: Trustworthiness
10-trustworthiness.summary: Inspiring confidence through consistent, honest, and reliable behaviour. Trustworthiness enables the BA to influence without authority and to gain the candid stakeholder input that quality requirements depend on.

11-organization-and-time-management.title: Organization and Time Management
11-organization-and-time-management.summary: Managing time, priorities, commitments, and resources effectively. Organization and time management ensure BA work is delivered predictably despite multiple competing demands.

12-adaptability.title: Adaptability
12-adaptability.summary: Adjusting to changing contexts, requirements, stakeholder needs, and methodologies. Adaptability is the ability to shift approach when circumstances demand it without losing effectiveness.

13-business-acumen.title: Business Acumen
13-business-acumen.summary: Understanding how enterprises create, deliver, and capture value. Business acumen connects BA work to business outcomes, enabling the BA to operate strategically rather than tactically.

14-industry-knowledge.title: Industry Knowledge
14-industry-knowledge.summary: Domain-specific knowledge — the terminology, regulations, processes, competitive dynamics, and standards of the industry in which the BA operates.

15-organization-knowledge.title: Organization Knowledge
15-organization-knowledge.summary: Knowledge of how the specific organization works — its culture, power structures, informal networks, policies, and political landscape.

16-solution-knowledge.title: Solution Knowledge
16-solution-knowledge.summary: Understanding of the solution domain — the technologies, products, processes, and methodologies relevant to the solutions the BA is specifying.

17-methodology-knowledge.title: Methodology Knowledge
17-methodology-knowledge.summary: Familiarity with BA methodologies (agile, waterfall, hybrid) and understanding when each is appropriate. Methodology knowledge enables the BA to design the right approach for each initiative.

18-verbal-communication.title: Verbal Communication
18-verbal-communication.summary: Clear, concise, audience-adapted speaking. Verbal communication is the primary channel for elicitation, facilitation, presentation, and stakeholder management.

19-non-verbal-communication.title: Non-Verbal Communication
19-non-verbal-communication.summary: Reading body language, tone, and presence; adjusting one's own non-verbal signals. Non-verbal communication often conveys more than words, especially in emotionally charged situations.

20-written-communication.title: Written Communication
20-written-communication.summary: Structured, unambiguous documentation tailored to the audience and purpose. Written communication produces the durable artefacts — requirements specs, business cases, stakeholder registers — that outlive verbal conversations.

21-listening.title: Listening
21-listening.summary: Active listening — hearing not just words but intent, concerns, and what is left unsaid. Paraphrasing to confirm understanding is the core practice.

22-facilitation.title: Facilitation
22-facilitation.summary: Guiding groups to productive outcomes without imposing personal views. Facilitation is the primary skill for workshops and collaborative sessions — it keeps groups focused, inclusive, and moving toward decisions.

23-leadership-and-influencing.title: Leadership and Influencing
23-leadership-and-influencing.summary: Influencing without formal authority — creating alignment around goals and motivating stakeholders to act. Leadership in BA means driving the analysis process forward even when the BA doesn't manage the team.

24-teamwork.title: Teamwork
24-teamwork.summary: Contributing to and supporting collaborative work — sharing credit, helping teammates, and putting team goals above individual recognition.

25-negotiation-and-conflict-resolution.title: Negotiation and Conflict Resolution
25-negotiation-and-conflict-resolution.summary: Finding mutually acceptable solutions to conflicting stakeholder needs. Negotiation and conflict resolution turn disagreement into productive compromise without damaging relationships.

26-teaching.title: Teaching
26-teaching.summary: Transferring knowledge to stakeholders and team members — enabling them to contribute more effectively to BA activities and to understand BA outputs.

27-office-productivity-tools-and-technol.title: Office Productivity Tools and Technology
27-office-productivity-tools-and-technol.summary: Proficient use of office productivity tools — word processors, spreadsheets, presentation software, diagramming tools. These are the foundational tools for documenting and communicating BA work.

28-business-analysis-tools-and-technolog.title: Business Analysis Tools and Technology
28-business-analysis-tools-and-technolog.summary: Specialized tools for BA work — requirements management platforms, modelling tools (BPMN, UML), wireframing and prototyping tools, and testing or traceability platforms.

29-communication-tools-and-technology.title: Communication Tools and Technology
29-communication-tools-and-technology.summary: Communication and collaboration platforms — email, video conferencing, instant messaging, wikis, shared document repositories, and project management tools.

30-acceptance-and-evaluation-criteria.title: Acceptance and Evaluation Criteria
30-acceptance-and-evaluation-criteria.summary: Defining conditions a solution must meet to be accepted by stakeholders. Acceptance criteria make requirements testable by establishing clear, verifiable conditions of satisfaction.

31-backlog-management.title: Backlog Management
31-backlog-management.summary: Maintaining and prioritizing a list of work items — the primary requirements management practice in agile contexts. Backlog management ensures the team always works on the most valuable items next.

32-balanced-scorecard.title: Balanced Scorecard
32-balanced-scorecard.summary: Strategic performance measurement across four perspectives: Financial, Customer, Internal Business Processes, and Learning & Growth. The Balanced Scorecard translates strategy into operational metrics.

33-benchmarking-and-market-analysis.title: Benchmarking and Market Analysis
33-benchmarking-and-market-analysis.summary: Comparing current performance, processes, or practices to industry standards, competitors, or best-in-class organizations. Benchmarking identifies performance gaps and improvement targets.

34-brainstorming.title: Brainstorming
34-brainstorming.summary: Divergent idea generation in a group setting. Key rules: defer judgment, go for quantity, encourage wild ideas, and build on others' ideas. Brainstorming is the starting point for creative problem solving.

35-business-capability-analysis.title: Business Capability Analysis
35-business-capability-analysis.summary: Mapping enterprise capabilities to identify strengths, gaps, and investment priorities. A business capability is what an enterprise does (not how it does it) — it is stable even as processes and systems change.

36-business-cases.title: Business Cases
36-business-cases.summary: Documenting the justification for a proposed initiative — analysing options, costs, benefits, risks, and recommending a course of action. The business case is the key decision-making document for investment approval.

37-business-model-canvas.title: Business Model Canvas
37-business-model-canvas.summary: Nine-block visual framework describing how an organization creates, delivers, and captures value: Key Partners, Key Activities, Key Resources, Value Propositions, Customer Relationships, Channels, Customer Segments, Cost Structure, Revenue Streams.

38-business-rules-analysis.title: Business Rules Analysis
38-business-rules-analysis.summary: Extracting and defining constraints and directives that govern organizational behaviour. Business rules are atomic statements about how the business operates — they are not processes or requirements but constraints on both.

39-collaborative-games.title: Collaborative Games
39-collaborative-games.summary: Structured activities that engage stakeholders creatively — Product Box, Buy a Feature, Speed Boat, and other facilitated games. Collaborative games surface requirements, priorities, and concerns in an engaging, low-inhibition format.

40-concept-modelling.title: Concept Modelling
40-concept-modelling.summary: Depicting key business concepts and their relationships — entity-relationship style but focused on business meaning, not data structures. Concept models build shared vocabulary across the organization.

41-data-dictionary.title: Data Dictionary
41-data-dictionary.summary: Cataloguing data elements with definitions, formats, allowable values, validation rules, and usage metadata. The Data Dictionary is the authoritative reference for data definitions across the enterprise.

42-data-flow-diagrams.title: Data Flow Diagrams
42-data-flow-diagrams.summary: Showing how data moves between processes, data stores, and external entities. Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs) provide a high-level view of data movement without revealing process details.

43-data-mining.title: Data Mining
43-data-mining.summary: Discovering patterns in large datasets to support decision making. Data mining uses statistical and machine learning techniques to identify correlations, clusters, and anomalies that humans would miss.

44-data-modelling.title: Data Modelling
44-data-modelling.summary: Designing logical and physical data structures using Entity Relationship Diagrams (ERDs) or class diagrams. Data modelling specifies the information the solution must manage.

45-decision-analysis.title: Decision Analysis
45-decision-analysis.summary: Evaluating choices under uncertainty — using decision trees, weighted ranking, or multi-criteria analysis to systematically compare alternatives.

46-decision-modelling.title: Decision Modelling
46-decision-modelling.summary: Representing complex decision logic using Decision Model and Notation (DMN). Decision models make business rules explicit, verifiable, and maintainable — replacing nested if-else logic with decision tables.

47-document-analysis.title: Document Analysis
47-document-analysis.summary: Reviewing existing documentation to extract requirements, understand current state, and identify constraints. Document analysis is the most efficient elicitation technique when relevant documentation exists.

48-estimation.title: Estimation
48-estimation.summary: Forecasting the effort, cost, or duration required for BA activities or solution delivery. Estimation techniques include analogous (based on similar past work), parametric (based on historical ratios), and three-point (optimistic, pessimistic, most likely).

49-financial-analysis.title: Financial Analysis
49-financial-analysis.summary: Quantifying the business value of solutions using ROI, Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), payback period, and cost-benefit analysis.

50-focus-groups.title: Focus Groups
50-focus-groups.summary: Guided discussion with 6-12 representative users to collect qualitative feedback, preferences, and perceptions about a system, process, or concept.

51-functional-decomposition.title: Functional Decomposition
51-functional-decomposition.summary: Breaking complex systems or processes into smaller, more manageable components. Functional decomposition creates a hierarchical view of what a system does, without describing how it does it.

52-glossary.title: Glossary
52-glossary.summary: Defining terms consistently to prevent misunderstanding across stakeholders. A glossary builds shared vocabulary, reducing ambiguity in requirements, communications, and deliverables.

53-interface-analysis.title: Interface Analysis
53-interface-analysis.summary: Identifying and documenting interactions between a system and its users or between systems. Interface analysis defines what crosses a solution boundary — inputs, outputs, data formats, and protocols.

54-interviews.title: Interviews
54-interviews.summary: Structured or unstructured one-on-one conversations with stakeholders. Interviews are the most flexible elicitation technique — adaptable to any stakeholder, topic, or context.

55-item-tracking.title: Item Tracking
55-item-tracking.summary: Logging and managing issues, defects, action items, and risks throughout the initiative. Item tracking ensures nothing falls through the cracks and provides an audit trail for decisions.

56-lessons-learned.title: Lessons Learned
56-lessons-learned.summary: Capturing what worked and what didn't from completed initiatives or phases. Lessons learned drive continuous improvement in BA practice and organizational capability.

57-metrics-and-key-performance-indicator.title: Metrics and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
57-metrics-and-key-performance-indicator.summary: Defining measurable performance indicators tied to business objectives. KPIs and metrics translate strategy into quantifiable targets that can be tracked over time.

58-mind-mapping.title: Mind Mapping
58-mind-mapping.summary: Non-linear visual brainstorming technique that captures ideas radiating from a central topic. Mind maps organize complex information in a way that mirrors how the brain naturally associates concepts.

59-non-functional-requirements-analysis.title: Non-Functional Requirements Analysis
59-non-functional-requirements-analysis.summary: Specifying quality attributes the solution must meet — performance, security, usability, reliability, availability, scalability, maintainability, and compliance. Non-functional requirements define 'how well' the system performs, not 'what' it does.

60-observation.title: Observation
60-observation.summary: Watching stakeholders perform their work (active or passive) to surface tacit knowledge — what people actually do versus what they say they do. Observation reveals workarounds, inefficiencies, and unstated needs.

61-organizational-modelling.title: Organizational Modelling
61-organizational-modelling.summary: Depicting roles, responsibilities, reporting structures, and organizational relationships. Organizational models (org charts, RACI matrices, role descriptions) clarify who does what and who decides what.

62-prioritization.title: Prioritization
62-prioritization.summary: Ranking requirements by relative importance using defined criteria. Prioritization enables the team to focus on the most valuable work first and make defensible scope trade-offs.

63-process-analysis.title: Process Analysis
63-process-analysis.summary: Examining existing processes to identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, redundancies, and improvement opportunities. Process analysis is the diagnostic phase that precedes process redesign.

64-process-modelling.title: Process Modelling
64-process-modelling.summary: Documenting business processes using BPMN, flowcharts, or swim-lane diagrams. Process models communicate how work flows across roles, systems, and departments.

65-prototyping.title: Prototyping
65-prototyping.summary: Creating working models of a solution to elicit requirements and validate understanding before full development. Prototypes make abstract requirements tangible.

66-reviews.title: Reviews
66-reviews.summary: Formal or informal examination of requirements documents, designs, or other BA work products for quality, completeness, and correctness. Reviews catch defects before they reach development.

67-risk-analysis-and-management.title: Risk Analysis and Management
67-risk-analysis-and-management.summary: Identifying, assessing, and planning responses to uncertainties that could affect the initiative. Risk analysis and management is proactive — it addresses what might go wrong before it does.

68-roles-and-permissions-matrix.title: Roles and Permissions Matrix
68-roles-and-permissions-matrix.summary: Mapping system functions to user roles and the permissions each role has. The Roles and Permissions Matrix (also called RACI for security) defines who can access, create, modify, or delete what.

69-root-cause-analysis.title: Root Cause Analysis
69-root-cause-analysis.summary: Finding the fundamental cause of a problem rather than treating symptoms. Root Cause Analysis uses techniques like 5 Whys (iteratively asking 'why' until the root cause emerges) and Fishbone/Ishikawa diagrams (categorizing potential causes by type).

70-scope-modelling.title: Scope Modelling
70-scope-modelling.summary: Defining and visualizing the boundaries of a solution — what is in scope and what is out. Scope modelling techniques include context diagrams (system and external entities), feature trees, and event-response lists.

71-sequence-diagrams.title: Sequence Diagrams
71-sequence-diagrams.summary: Modelling object or system interactions in time sequence using UML Sequence Diagrams. Sequence diagrams show the order of messages exchanged between participants to accomplish a function.

72-stakeholder-list-map-or-personas.title: Stakeholder List, Map, or Personas
72-stakeholder-list-map-or-personas.summary: Identifying and characterizing stakeholders to plan engagement and understand their needs, influence, and attitudes. Deliverables include stakeholder lists, maps (Power/Interest Grid), and personas.

73-state-modelling.title: State Modelling
73-state-modelling.summary: Depicting the states an object can occupy and the valid transitions between them. State modelling (UML State Machine Diagrams) reveals complex object behaviour that flow-based models miss.

74-survey-or-questionnaire.title: Survey or Questionnaire
74-survey-or-questionnaire.summary: Collecting structured input from many stakeholders through standardized questions. Surveys and questionnaires are the most efficient way to gather data from large or geographically distributed groups.

75-swot-analysis.title: SWOT Analysis
75-swot-analysis.summary: Strategic assessment of Strengths (internal positive), Weaknesses (internal negative), Opportunities (external positive), and Threats (external negative). SWOT provides a structured situational analysis for decision making.

76-use-cases-and-scenarios.title: Use Cases and Scenarios
76-use-cases-and-scenarios.summary: Describing interactions between actors (users, systems, organizations) and the system to achieve a specific goal. Use cases capture functional requirements as a sequence of interactions with clear outcomes.

77-user-stories.title: User Stories
77-user-stories.summary: Short, structured expressions of user need: 'As a [role], I want [goal] so that [benefit].' User stories are placeholders for conversation, not full requirements — they shift the focus from documenting to discussing.

78-vendor-assessment.title: Vendor Assessment
78-vendor-assessment.summary: Evaluating third-party vendors against defined requirements and criteria. Vendor assessment includes market research, RFP/RFQ, vendor demonstrations, reference checks, and pilot evaluations.

79-workshops.title: Workshops
79-workshops.summary: Facilitated group sessions that engage cross-functional stakeholders in eliciting, analysing, or validating requirements. Workshops are the most powerful elicitation technique for complex, multi-stakeholder requirements.

80-the-agile-perspective.title: The Agile Perspective
80-the-agile-perspective.summary: A just-in-time analysis approach — deliver the right detail at the right time, not everything upfront. The BA operates as a continuous team member, refining requirements iteratively through the product backlog.

81-the-business-intelligence-perspective.title: The Business Intelligence Perspective
81-the-business-intelligence-perspective.summary: Enabling data-driven decision making through information quality, architecture, and analytics. The BA focus shifts from process requirements to data requirements — definitions, quality, lineage, and governance.

82-the-information-technology-perspectiv.title: The Information Technology Perspective
82-the-information-technology-perspectiv.summary: Bridging business needs and technical solutions within IT delivery contexts. The BA translates business language into precise system requirements without over-specifying implementation.

83-the-business-architecture-perspective.title: The Business Architecture Perspective
83-the-business-architecture-perspective.summary: Aligning change initiatives with enterprise capabilities, strategy, and operating model. The BA works at the enterprise level, analysing capability gaps, value streams, and strategic alignment.

84-the-business-process-management-persp.title: The Business Process Management Perspective
84-the-business-process-management-persp.summary: Analyzing, modelling, optimizing, and managing business processes as a core deliverable. The BA focuses on process discovery, analysis, redesign, and governance using BPMN (Business Process Model and Notation).
